notes.title: The Bus DLC – Hamburg City – New Neighborhoods in Hamburg City
notes.notes:
[h3]The Bus DLC – Hamburg City – New Residential Buildings for the Northern Expansion[/h3][p]With the free extension of bus lines 6 and 17 to the north, new residential areas are also arriving in the game. Instead of dense inner-city blocks, you’ll now encounter more open neighborhoods featuring single-family homes, smaller apartment buildings, and even garden allotments – all in true North German style.[/p][p]To authentically recreate this variety, [i]The Bus[/i] makes use of so-called [b]Blueprints[/b]. These are modular construction kits within Unreal Engine that allow objects to be assembled from many individual parts.
We’ve already used this method to create numerous variations of shelters and signposts – and now buildings are joining the lineup.[/p][p]For the northern expansion, we’ve developed two brand-new Blueprints:[/p][list][*][p][b]Residential Houses:[/b] Different building shapes, roof types, doors, windows, façade colors, and extras like balconies or solar panels ensure that every house is unique.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Garden Allotments:[/b] No two sheds look the same here either. Thanks to the special Blueprint, countless variations of small garden houses appear – just like you’d find in Hamburg’s neighborhoods.[/p][/*][/list][p]The advantage: while creating a Blueprint takes a little longer, it allows us to generate a huge variety of new objects in no time. This not only adds variety and saves development effort but also brings the northern districts of Hamburg to life with a realistic look.[/p][p]At the end of this post, you’ll find some work-in-progress images showing just how different these procedurally built houses can appear. You’ll soon spot them along the new lines 7 and 277.[/p][p]And don’t forget:
The big [b]Aerosoft Publisher Sale[/b] runs until September 23, 2025, 7 PM CEST!
You can grab [i]The Bus DLC – Hamburg City[/i] with a [b]25% discount[/b] – a great chance to experience virtual Hamburg. All upcoming line expansions are, of course, included for free.[/p][p][b]Stay up to date:[/b]
Follow us on Facebook or subscribe to our newsletter. For instant updates, join our Telegram channel and get all the news directly on your smartphone.[/p][p]We hope you continue to enjoy your time in Hamburg![/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Steam Store Page[/b]

notes.title: The Bus Hamburg City – Updates on line 7
notes.notes:
[p]While one part of the development team continues working on the already released lines 6 and 17 — addressing community feedback and adding new features like AI buses — another part is focusing on the northern expansion.[/p][p][/p][p]The new line 7 runs from Barmbek station towards Steilshoop. Along the way, it shows many faces of the city: from Barmbek’s lively center with shops and restaurants, through commercial areas, to the distinctive high-rise buildings in Steilshoop. Despite the dense urban development, the district is surprisingly green and varied.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/7557aad2e62e9bfad122a7d7af6c4305c109acbb.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/9112d51b775ccc6ae04d9ed570f2aa4dd97c6086.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/690dda3a29239fea3958fd48de1041189da99534.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Many new buildings are being created as individual 3D models. Highlights include the Catholic Church of St. Johannis on Gründgensstraße, the Emil-Krause School near Habichtstraße subway station, and modern single-family homes near the Borchertring terminus. Of course, the typical four-story red brick apartment buildings are also included.[/p][p][/p][p]Particularly charming are the allotment gardens with wooden garden sheds, which have not appeared in the Hamburg DLC before. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/9701c4bf5b12439df0fa58c1adce1b4a36da1c7a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/d3b28731c6ec28e4f7204a78b4af3419d50a210c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]A new line means more than just new buildings. It also brings new streets, pathways, markings, traffic signs, and countless small details. While one part of the team focuses on buildings, another works on roads, sidewalks, curbs, and traffic rules. After that comes vegetation, lighting, and many tiny objects that are hardly noticed but are crucial for the atmosphere.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/cfc0732281266237d6cd2d57e0fd6c7b829feaae.jpg"][/img] [/p][p]The images in this news post give a first impression of the current progress. Many buildings are already placed but will be further refined and aligned correctly. Some screenshots also show maps from the State Survey Office (Geoportal), which allow us to achieve almost centimeter-accurate placement. [/p][p]Please note: this is development material and will continue to be expanded.[/p][p]
[/p][p]If you have any questions, suggestions, or feedback about The Bus DLC Hamburg City, feel free to reach out to us at [url="mailto:TheBus@halycon.info"]TheBus@halycon.info[/url]. We’re always happy to hear from you![/p][p]Stay up to date:[/p][list][*][p]Follow us on Facebook[/p][/*][*][p]Subscribe to our newsletter[/p][/*][*][p]Or get updates even faster via our Telegram channel with push notifications straight to your smartphone[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]We hope you continue to enjoy exploring virtual Hamburg![/p]

notes.title: The Bus DLC Hamburg City – New version available
notes.notes:
[p]The new version of the popular [i]The Bus[/i] DLC [b]Hamburg City[/b] is now available on Steam![/p][p]
A huge thank you to our community—many of your suggestions and requests have been included in this update.[/p][p]Of course, not everything can be implemented right away. Adjustments to bus mods are still limited, as there isn’t a usable vehicle editor yet.
New buses aren’t part of the Hamburg DLC itself, since in [i]The Bus[/i], vehicles and maps are separate content.
However, Steam bundles that combine both could be possible in the future.[/p][p][/p][h3]What’s new in this version?[/h3][p]The most noticeable change is the many new Hamburg lamps and streetlights.
Over ten new variants have been added, from whip lights in different shapes to double masts with spotlights and new lighting on traffic islands.
This makes Hamburg’s streets even more atmospheric at night. Check out the comparison images of old vs. new lighting in this news post.[/p][p]Announcements have also been expanded and refined, for example at terminal stops and transfer points.
Plus, new city details have been added, like the blue crane in front of the Museum of Work in Barmbek. Even if the bus doesn’t pass directly by, it adds to the authentic atmosphere.
Timetables and fleet files have been updated, and some objects now have improved collision detection.[/p][p][/p][h3]Looking ahead[/h3][p]We’re already working on more features, including AI buses on lines 6 and 17, which are currently being tested in the base game.
The northern route extension with line 7 is also in progress, and we’ll share more details soon. The updated lighting will, of course, be included on this new section as well.[/p][p][/p][h3]Changelog[/h3][list][*][p]New Hamburg lamps and streetlights[/p][/*][*][p]Added announcements for transfer points[/p][/*][*][p]English announcements added at the main station[/p][/*][*][p]Travel times from depot to starting stop adjusted[/p][/*][*][p]Fleet file updates[/p][/*][*][p]Improved collision detection for objects[/p][/*][*][p]New objects, e.g., historic crane at the Museum of Work in Barmbek[/p][/*][*][p]Corrections to terminal stop announcements[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Steam Update[/h3][p]The update will be delivered automatically via Steam. Depending on your settings, it may download immediately or later.
If you don’t want to wait, you can start the download manually by clicking the button next to the entry in the Steam client.
New players will, of course, receive the latest version right away.[/p][p][/p][h3]Stay connected[/h3][p]Follow us on Facebook or subscribe to our newsletter to stay up to date. notes.title: The Bus DLC – Hamburg City – Preview of Upcoming Updates
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/ef03b84d4a8bebf861b359fe01f6e902e26e23c6.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Since the end of July, the popular Hamburg map for [i]The Bus[/i] has been available, and work on it is continuing at full speed.[/p][p]We have carefully evaluated the feedback from Steam comments, YouTube videos, and directly through the TML reporting system.[/p][p][/p][p]At this point, we would like to sincerely thank you for your numerous ideas, suggestions, remarks, as well as for your praise and constructive criticism.[/p][p][/p][h3]More Variety in Street Lamps[/h3][p]One point of criticism concerned the street lighting.[/p][p]For Hamburg, we had already implemented special details, such as the lamps hanging on cables in Steinstraße and at Steintorbrücke, or the spotlights on the warehouse buildings.
However, in reality, Hamburg’s street lamp landscape is even more diverse.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s why, since release, we have created over ten additional models and variants, which will gradually replace the previous lamps.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/4cf2c81f580c72965edf5df1dd14e4720f6e1376.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]For example, at Sandtorkai you will now find the typical whip-shaped double lamps, and at major intersections, new tall lanterns will be used in the future.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/23d6453d1f00690d84bffdcf4b79899b69772b27.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]All lamps have also been optimized in terms of their light cones to create a coherent night-time appearance.
The wide variety of different heights and light fixtures will also be visible on the upcoming section of Line 7.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/d6c688bb068fefc8838ed9a6c9d0317c81784abc.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Progress on the AI Buses[/h3][p]Progress is also being made with the AI buses.[/p][p]The implementation is technically complex, since the tests cannot be carried out directly in the editor, but instead in a special internal game version that has to be generated anew each time.[/p][p]As the AI buses are still in the beta phase in the main game, patience is required – but we want to make this feature available for Hamburg as soon as possible.[/p][p][/p][h3]Outlook[/h3][p]The next update for [i]The Bus[/i] DLC – [b]Hamburg City[/b] is scheduled for August 2025.
As soon as it becomes available, we will publish a news post with the full changelog.
You can already find the first images at the end of this announcement.[/p][p][/p][h3]Stay Up to Date[/h3][p]Follow us on Facebook or subscribe to our newsletter to never miss any news.[/p][p]For even quicker updates, join our Telegram channel – there you will receive all information directly as push notifications on your smartphone.[/p][p][/p][p]We wish you continued fun in virtual Hamburg![/p]

notes.title: The Bus DLC Hamburg City - News on the route expansion!
notes.notes:
[p]Anyone who has closely followed our recent announcement about the future of [i]The Bus[/i] DLC – Hamburg City might have already spotted a small hint in the news image about what’s to come:[/p][p][b]In [i]The Bus[/i] DLC – Hamburg City, Line 7 heads north![/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/df55a9f4f476a987bb694b011745bcdc35d16733.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The map is being expanded, and work on it is already in full swing.[/p][p]The new route will run from the Barmbek U- and S-Bahn station further north.
The roundabout there could already be seen in the announcement image.
North of the roundabout, several lines run further into the north, and one of them – Line 7 – is now being built.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/87be55f01c1a4b6c1c1224926f6b1c9658c67db5.jpg"][/img]  [/p][p]Line 7 will end in Steilshoop. This district, part of the Wandsbek borough, has many faces.
On one hand, from the late 1960s onwards, high-rise housing was built here for more than 20,000 people; on the other, it is also a green oasis with parks, abundant trees, sports facilities, and allotment gardens.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/35bd85448425b9cc694e12781109082af9396677.jpg"][/img]  [/p][p]Here, too, Hamburg lives up to its reputation as a very green city.[/p][p]The journey on Line 7 takes you through the more urban Barmbek area, past shops, restaurants, residential areas, and commercial zones, towards Steilshooper Allee.
After a short stretch there, the bus turns east into Gustav-Seitz-Weg.
It then passes through a roundabout from which parts of the Steilshoop shopping center can be seen, and continues into Gründgensstraße, named after German actor Gustav Gründgens.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/b3f52c1c0d1992159a5f5c631373bc0911ef4d71.jpg"][/img]  [/p][p]Shortly before Borchertring, the bus reaches its terminus, also called Borchertring.
There, the bus has its own loop with a layover area, providing enough space to turn around before starting the return trip to Barmbek.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/3b1eb6ddceee493923e54c7a8c7d767b517b85fe.jpg"][/img]  [/p][p][/p]

notes.title: The Bus DLC Hamburg City - AI Bus news!
notes.notes:
[p]We are continuously working on our popular [b]Hamburg City DLC[/b] for [i]The Bus[/i].[/p][p][/p][p]Since it’s an add-on, some features depend on expansions to the main game – and one particularly exciting topic is the [b]AI buses[/b] you will encounter along your routes.[/p][p]In the current beta version of [i]The Bus[/i], AI buses are now available for all Public Beta players in Berlin to test.
At the moment, however, this only applies to the main game with the Berlin bus lines – the Hamburg area has not yet been integrated.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Why AI buses in Hamburg still need to wait[/b][/p][p]Currently, using AI buses on Hamburg lines leads to numerous issues:[/p][list][*][p]AI bus drivers get stuck at objects they could otherwise avoid[/p][/*][*][p]Some turn incorrectly or take curves unnaturally[/p][/*][*][p]Certain paths are not used as expected[/p][/*][/list][p]Behind the scenes, adapting the AI buses requires extensive work: roadside objects, other AI vehicles, and special driving paths all need to be checked, changed, and optimised – and this for each bus individually.[/p][p]We are also currently working with a different editor version than in Berlin, which requires additional adjustments and unfortunately takes time.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Important note for the Public Beta[/b][/p][p]In the current beta version of the main game, there are some route errors on the Hamburg map, such as missing road sections, absent curbs, and gaps or incorrect areas on pavements.
These problems are caused by the different versions of the main game and the add-on.[/p][p]Our recommendation: [b]Do not play Hamburg City in the Public Beta at the moment[/b] to avoid these issues.[/p][p][b]Looking ahead[/b][/p][p]Once the adjustments are complete, your virtual colleagues will automatically be running on Hamburg’s [b]lines 6 and 17[/b].
Intersecting lines will not be possible at first, but they are planned for a later main game update – and will then also be implemented in Hamburg.[/p][p][/p][p]Further information on the work on the virtual Hamburg map will follow soon.
Stay tuned – and until then, we hope you continue to enjoy your time in the northern German metropolis with [i]The Bus[/i]![/p]

notes.title: The Bus DLC Hamburg City – What’s Next?
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/2066e6545c647b5f608bcf2cdc4606bf21372fa5.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]The Bus DLC Hamburg City – What’s Next? [/h3][p]With the release of our first expansion for the bus simulator [i]The Bus[/i], the Hamburg chapter is far from over – quite the opposite! Today, we’d like to give you a brief update on what’s happening behind the scenes and what you can look forward to next. [/p][p][/p][h3]Bug Fixes & Fine-Tuning [/h3][p]Since the release, we’ve continued to receive valuable reports via TML’s reporting system – thank you to everyone contributing! Some of these reports relate to the DLC itself, while others concern the base game. We carefully review each message and are working continuously to fix issues and implement improvements in upcoming updates. [/p][p][/p][h3]AI Buses in the Pipeline [/h3][p]The next big step is just around the corner: TML will soon include the feature for AI-controlled buses in a beta version of the game. Then it's time for us to test – especially on the Hamburg lines! [/p][p]Particular attention will be paid to challenging spots like the turning loop at Borgweg – a real test of skill, even for human drivers. Winterhude also features some tight sections that need close inspection and, if necessary, adjustments to the AI paths. Our goal: a smooth and realistic AI driving experience throughout the map. [/p][p]Once the AI buses are running flawlessly, they’ll arrive in Hamburg with a future update – as soon as TML officially enables the feature. [/p][p][/p][h3]Looking Ahead [/h3][p]Many of you have asked whether there will be further expansions for the Hamburg map after release. The answer is: yes! [/p][p]We’re continuing to work on the map beyond bug fixes, with new content and ideas already being evaluated. Some plans have been in place since the start of the project, others are currently being reviewed for feasibility. Once we’re ready to reveal more, we’ll be sure to let you know! [/p][p][/p][h3]What About New Buses? [/h3][p]At the moment, we’re not planning to add new drivable buses to the game through this DLC. In [i]The Bus[/i], maps and buses are released as separate expansions. That said, bundles via Steam could be a possibility in the future – once a dedicated bus editor becomes available. For now, a bus DLC isn’t feasible without the necessary tools. [/p][p][/p][h3]Stay Tuned! [/h3][p]So yes – things are still moving forward in Hamburg! [/p][p]To stay up to date, follow us on Facebook, subscribe to our Telegram channel, or check our website regularly. [/p][p][/p][p]We’re excited to continue this journey together with you![/p]

[p]In this entry of our developer diary, we’re heading back to Barmbek Station.
We first introduced the 3D model of the station building in [i]Developer Diary #54[/i]. This time, we have much more to show you: the station has now been fully integrated into the game world, and the entire surrounding area has been carefully designed.[/p][p]For those interested in the historical background of Barmbek Station, you’ll find a link to our earlier post at the end of this article.[/p][p][/p][h3]Barmbek Station Comes to Life[/h3][p]The station is now completely embedded into the map. The surrounding streets have been laid out, numerous nearby buildings have been constructed, and countless details have been added to bring the area to life.[/p][p]One special feature: from bus line 17, players can clearly see the elevated tracks where local trains pass above. Both the U3 subway line and the S1 suburban railway are featured as AI-controlled trains, recreated in their characteristic Hamburg style especially for the DLC.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/1867284e9f71709b3c0f6a1a6f7a130ec350f548.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]A Major Transportation Hub[/h3][p]Just like in real life, Barmbek Station serves as a major transport hub where the subway, suburban rail, and various bus lines intersect. For the bus lines that terminate here, we’ve added lay-bys in the northern section on Krüsistraße, complete with static buses to bring authenticity to the scene.[/p][p]To faithfully recreate the station area, many 3D assets had to be custom modeled. This includes not only the station itself—its entrances, platforms, and buildings—but also the distinctive brick structures along Krüsistraße, the well-known outdoor retailer on the south side near the round bunker, all bridge constructions to the east and west, and numerous other buildings typical of the neighborhood.[/p][p]As in the real-world counterpart, the station is built on an embankment, with tracks running high above street level.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/699e691ac0be6caaa64fe0d2f4bb5fb6fc3135e1.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Crafted with Attention to Detail[/h3][p]You can see many of these elements in the screenshots provided: furnished waiting areas, roundabouts, market squares, signage, road markings, and more—all designed with great care and attention to detail.[/p][p]Please note that the images are from a work-in-progress version. We’re still refining many small elements to breathe even more life into the entire area.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/e41ebce11c523c89a384ef917e166e6aa387fac1.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Stay Up to Date[/h3][p]You can now find more information and additional screenshots of the DLC on the newly launched Steam product page.

notes.title: The Bus – Hamburg DLC | FAQs – Frequently Asked Questions Part 2
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/01dfedc69e5d0e67acf977fdbd2d7d98f0daaaf7.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]A few weeks ago, we published the first part of our Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) about the upcoming Hamburg City DLC for [i]The Bus[/i] and invited you to send us more questions. You certainly did – thank you for your continued interest![/b][/p][p]Before we dive into the new answers, we want to emphasize once again: the Hamburg expansion is being developed independently by us, Halycon Media, as a third-party developer. The development of the main game [i]The Bus[/i] remains with TML-Studios.
That means we unfortunately cannot provide information on topics such as future AI lines or multiplayer changes in the base game. For those, please reach out to TML directly.[/p][p]What we [i]can[/i] say: as soon as new features become available in the main game, we will of course assess whether and how they can be integrated into our Hamburg DLC through an update.[/p][p]Do you have more questions, suggestions, or ideas? Feel free to email us at [b]TheBus@halycon.info[/b] with the subject line “FAQ”. We’ll continue updating the list regularly until release.[/p][p]And now – enjoy part two of the Frequently Asked Questions for [i]The Bus DLC – Hamburg City[/i]![/p][p][/p][p][b]Your Halycon Media Team[/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]FAQs – Part 2 / As of: June 12, 2025[/b] [/p][list][*][p][b]When will the Hamburg City DLC for The Bus be released?[/b] 
There is still no fixed release date, but one thing’s for sure: it won’t be much longer! [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]How much will the add-on cost?[/b] 
Hamburg City is a paid expansion. Since March 2023, a team of up to 15 people has been working on it. The final price will be announced at a later date. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Can you get off the bus and enter buildings?[/b] 
A charming idea – and one we’ve also considered, for example as hidden “Easter eggs” inside certain buildings. However, the technical and creative effort involved is very high. That’s why, for now, we’re focusing on route design and surroundings. But who knows what the future holds? [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Will the map be developed further after release?[/b] 
Yes. We’ll continue working on the Hamburg City map even after release. 
In addition to potential bug fixes, new features from the main game (such as AI bus lines or engine updates) may require changes to the map. We will evaluate these and, if needed, implement them through updates. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Will there be additional Hamburg-specific AI vehicles?[/b] 
Yes! In addition to typical waste collection trucks, which look noticeably different in Hamburg compared to those in Berlin, several regional vehicles will be added. Details will follow in a future news post. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Is there a bus depot in the game?[/b] 
The real Alsterdorf depot is located up to 10 km away from the route’s starting point, which would require building an entirely new section. Therefore, we’ve chosen alternative pause and parking areas for release: such as the bays on Feldstraße near the bunker, parking lots on Willy-Brandt-Allee, and the bus terminal behind the central station (ZOB). All of these exist in real life. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Will there be additional buses specifically for the Hamburg map?[/b] 
Whether we’ll release buses tailored to the Hamburg City map remains to be seen. Currently, there’s no vehicle editor available for us to create them ourselves. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Is Halycon planning more maps for The Bus?[/b] 
Since announcing the Hamburg DLC, we’ve received many exciting suggestions. However, selecting future projects depends on numerous factors. 
Our current focus is entirely on Hamburg – but we’ve already begun internally evaluating potential next cities. As soon as we have news, you’ll hear it here first. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Why does the eCitaro include a BVG (Berlin) ticket validator? Will it be replaced?[/b] 
TML plans to address this in future versions. Once the base game allows it, we’ll update the Hamburg Hochbahn bus mod accordingly. For now, the eCitaro is already customized with Hochbahn-style paintwork, red seat upholstery, and appropriate matrix and interior displays. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]What time period does the Hamburg DLC represent?[/b] 
The implementation is based on the conditions of spring 2023 – including street layouts, buildings, route alignments, and bus stops. In a major city like Hamburg, constant changes are the norm, which is why we’ve locked the DLC to a fixed reference point. This is especially noticeable around stops like Saarlandstraße. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]Will there be additional repaints besides the eCitaro and Galaxis?[/b] 
Yes, we plan to provide Hochbahn-style liveries for all currently available bus models in [i]The Bus[/i] – even if those particular buses were never used in Hamburg. This is intended to make things easier for players when choosing vehicles. [/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: The Bus Hamburg City DLC | Developer-Diary #75

notes.notes:
This week, we’re taking you on a special tour:
Instead of focusing on a single building or road section, we’re showcasing impressions from across the entire route network of the upcoming Hamburg City DLC for The Bus.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/487287bebdd2c9c6e02a8437209782d6b139ce4c.png[/img]

These screenshots are taken from both Line 6 and Line 17, offering a first glimpse at the variety of route segments awaiting you in the finished add-on.

As always, please note: everything you see here is still under development.
Road surfaces, manhole covers, traffic signs, stop equipment – all these elements are still being carefully optimized and refined.
Still, the images already give a good impression of how detailed and atmospheric the virtual recreation of Hamburg is becoming.

[u]Some iconic sections of Line 6:[/u]

[list]
[*] Speicherstadt with the world-famous Miniatur Wunderland, the starting stop of Line 6, and a unique mix of heritage-listed warehouses and modern architecture.
[*] St. Peter’s Church at Domplatz, including the distinctive red temporary bus stops.
[*] Central Station and its surroundings – a key hub where many lines will eventually intersect – featuring iconic buildings like the Schauspielhaus, the Bieberhaus, and the Museum of Arts and Crafts.
[*] Lange Reihe, a narrow, bustling street with a traditional weekly market.
[*] Major construction site at Sechslingspforte, right by the Binnenalster.
[*] Residential areas such as Mühlenkamp, Goldbekplatz, and Jarresstraße, characterized by typical red-brick architecture in the style of Hamburg’s northern districts.
[*] The green route to Borgweg, the terminus of Line 6, which is also part of Line 17.
[/list]

[u]In addition, Line 17 follows its own unique route – with even more highlights:[/u]

[list]
[*] Feldstraße with the Rindermarkthalle, Heiligengeistfeld, and the green-topped bunker, now housing a hotel, restaurants, and a concert hall.
[*] Millerntor Stadium and the iconic Knappschaft building, home to the legendary Zwick pub and the adjacent Dancing Towers.
[*] St. Michael’s Church, known as “Michel” – a true landmark of the city that Line 17 passes right by.
[*] Rödingsmarkt station, where animated subway trains will be visible in the future.
[*] The Zurich building on Domstraße, with a bus stop directly in front and a view into the green interior courtyard.
[*] Saarlandstraße station, with a large EDEKA supermarket right at the Wiesendamm intersection.
[*] Barmbek station, featuring roundabouts, a circular bunker, and passenger facilities on both sides of the street.
[/list]
Each of these locations tells a piece of Hamburg’s urban history, and we’re doing our best to make that digitally tangible.
The route layout connects historical landmarks with everyday city life, modern residential areas with bustling shopping streets – always with attention to the big picture as well as the smallest details.

notes.title: The Bus DLC Hamburg | FAQs - Frequently asked questions | Updated on 8/4/25
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/a71f22331c48899964072d3066949063910524e7.jpg"][/img]A list of frequently asked questions and answers for the upcoming dlc Hamburg City, created by third party developer (independent external developer) of that AddOn Halycon Media. [/p][p]
-[i]Updated on August 4 2025[/i] -[/p][p][/p][h3]When will the Hamburg City DLC for The Bus be released?[/h3][p]There is no fixed release date yet. However, we can say this much: it won’t be much longer! You can look forward to the launch very soon. 


[/p][h3]How much will the add-on cost? [/h3][p]Hamburg City is a paid expansion for The Bus. Since March 2023, a dedicated team of up to 15 people has been working on its development. The final price will be announced at a later date. 


[/p][h3]Will AI characters and vehicles be adjusted? [/h3][p]The core behavior of AI vehicles and pedestrians is based on The Bus's main game standards and can only be modified within limited technical constraints. Any adjustments will be made within the possibilities offered by the base game. 


[/p][h3]Can Hamburg City be played in multiplayer mode? [/h3][p]Yes! Since The Bus supports multiplayer, the Hamburg City map is also playable in multiplayer mode. All players must own the same DLCs to use them together. 


[/p][h3]Will there be AI-controlled bus traffic? [/h3][p]As long as the main game does not support AI bus routes, this feature cannot be implemented on the Hamburg City map either. 
However, if The Bus introduces this feature in the future, we will provide an appropriate update. Timetables for AI routes are already prepared — and hubs like the central station are expected to feature busy AI traffic once activated. 


[/p][h3]Will a bus be included – and if so, which one? [/h3][p]In contrast to other bus simulators such as OMSI2, maps and buses are separate in The Bus. This means that a map does not necessarily include one or more buses.
An original elevated railway bus from the real fleet in Hamburg is therefore not included in the scope of delivery, in addition to the buses known from the main game.
In addition, there is currently no vehicle editor available for buses, which means that it is not technically possible to create another drivable elevated railway bus yourself. It has not yet been decided whether we will release buses as a separate add-on in the future.
What we will deliver, however, are adaptations of existing standard buses, for example paintwork, seat upholstery, interior displays and matrix. More information on this will follow later.


[/p][h3]Why develop a DLC while the main game is still in Early Access? [/h3][p]The main game The Bus is being developed solely by TML-Studios. 
We are responsible for the Hamburg City map expansion, which adds a new city and additional routes to the game. 
We have no influence on the development or feature set of the main game and cannot introduce core changes. 
Important: Work on Hamburg City does not interfere with the development of The Bus — these are separate teams working independently. 


[/p][h3]Are the Hochbahn buses shown in the screenshots functional AI vehicles? [/h3][p]No. The Hochbahn buses currently visible in work-in-progress screenshots are static objects — placed at rest areas, for example — and serve to enhance the map's authenticity. 
They are neither drivable nor AI-controlled. 


[/p][h3]Will Line 17 be extended to U-Bahn station Berne? [/h3][p]We are currently discussing internal plans to extend Line 17 by another 10 km to the Berne underground station. The potential route would be very varied – it passes through various residential areas, from red post-war brick buildings to high-rise estates and 1970s architecture to over 100-year-old housing estates, complemented by parks, new housing developments and many intersections. Implementing this section is likely to take some time, given the current level of quality. [/p][p]However, there are also other options for expanding the map in a meaningful way. [/p][p]The decision-making and planning process is already underway.  


[/p][h3]Will there be more bus lines added to the Hamburg DLC in the future? [/h3][p]Additional lines are an option that we are considering. They must be compatible with the existing DLC and be able to be implemented within a reasonable time frame.


[/p][h3]Are typical Hamburg rail vehicles featured in the game?[/h3][p]Yes! The Hamburg City map offers a vibrant cityscape featuring many iconic rail vehicles. 
In addition to DT5 Hamburg U-Bahn trains, you’ll also see S-Bahn, Metronom, regional, and long-distance trains as AI traffic — realistically placed along their real-life routes. 
For example, at Rödingsmarkt station, U-Bahn trains cross above Line 17, while at Barmbek you’ll see S-Bahn trains, and the central station showcases all train types. 


[/p][h3]Will the Hamburg expansion be released for consoles? [/h3][p]Yes – the Hamburg City map is planned for consoles as well, once the main game becomes available on those platforms. 
However, we cannot yet provide a specific release date.[/p]

notes.title: The Bus - DLC Hamburg - Developer Diary
notes.notes:
This week, we are focusing on an interesting section of the route network in The Bus DLC - Hamburg City, Saarlandstraße.
A place that, despite its rather quiet location in the game, catches the eye with its striking architecture and proximity to the subway station.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/09e4c7893701b5885060955d7ba825132983ae1b.jpg[/img]


Even though bus route 17 does not pass directly by the station in the simulation, there is a clear view of the striking station and the adjacent bridge structures from the intersection at Wiesendamm.
This visual presence was reason enough for us to integrate the area into the game true to the original - including a small special feature: at irregular intervals, a Hamburg subway train will also be seen crossing the bridge, providing additional dynamics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/1eadfdd3685572cb2f9fe466535437c4eb844574.jpg[/img]

As usual, the images shown are from the current development phase. Some elements - especially the signage - still serve as placeholders, but they already convey an atmospheric impression of the surroundings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/58e238b3b35926c9a0903762108119c528343e2d.jpg[/img]

The subway station was opened in 1912 and is part of the U3 ring line, one of Hamburg's oldest subway lines.
The station has only borne the name Saarlandstraße since 1970 and was previously called Bahnhof Stadtpark.

The station is located above ground on an embankment with a striking steel bridge over Saarlandstraße and the Barmbeker Strichkanal to the east.
This is a typical feature of Hamburg's elevated railway architecture of the time. The station was named after the street of the same name, which in turn was named after Saarland in the 1920s.
In the early days, the station was an important transfer point for workers from the surrounding residential and industrial areas, who found connections to the city center here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/e8b8ece8bd86ce0a05a79b4ea42ca4eee178db13.jpg[/img]

Today, Saarlandstraße is no longer a classic transportation hub, but it remains an important part of the U3.
It connects the Winterhude district with the rest of the Hochbahn network and is particularly popular with commuters and residents.
Its proximity to the Alster, Stadtpark and Jarrestraße also makes the area attractive for leisure trips.
The architecture of the station with the adjoining railroad bridges has been largely preserved in its original state to this day and is a listed building. This makes the area not only functional, but also remarkable from an architectural and historical point of view.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/a3c636f0bbee0cfdf5a499bd78f150095ca021a0.jpg[/img]

In the virtual realization, we attach particular importance to the depiction of the characteristic brick facades, the curved bridge structure and the typical signal and traffic lights.

All of this contributes to creating an authentic cityscape that Hamburgers will immediately recognize - and that will also make newcomers want to explore the city digitally.

Do you have any questions, suggestions or requests for upcoming topics?

Then write to us as always: TheBus@halycon.info

See you next time - and have fun exploring Hamburg in The Bus!

notes.title: The Bus - DLC Hamburg - Developer diary
notes.notes:
This week, we are taking a look at one of the most famous and at the same time most complex buildings in the Hanseatic city: Hamburg Central Station.
With over 500,000 passengers a day, it is one of the busiest train stations in Europe - and is therefore also a central part of the route network in The Bus DLC - Hamburg City.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/bcc0c5c7adae15ddc708918ccd65be7876fdc789.jpg[/img]

In the simulation, the bus routes run along the Steintorwall and Steintordamm - i.e. directly alongside the main station.
The bus stops are located directly at the pedestrian exits to the platforms, which makes for a particularly realistic transfer scenario.
Even though many of the platform details are not directly visible from above, it was important to us to recreate them true to the original in order to make the atmosphere of the location tangible.

As always, the images shown are from a development phase that has not yet been finalized.
The overhead line is currently still being reworked, as are the platform areas, which will later be supplemented with suitable decorations and other objects.
In the finished game, regional trains, Metronom trains and even a few long-distance trains will be seen there alongside suburban trains - some of which will be visible from the street, making them a real eye-catcher in the cityscape.

A look at the history of the main station shows how deeply rooted this transportation hub is in urban life:
The station was opened in 1906 and replaced several smaller terminus stations.
The imposing steel and glass hall construction was an architectural masterpiece in its day - and remains so to this day.
The track layout is characterized by its central location: connections branch out from here in all directions - from the city centre to the suburbs, from northern Germany to the south.

This networking is also noticeable in the simulation. The area around the main station represents a kind of heart of the route, both in terms of passenger flows and from a transport planning perspective.
The digital implementation is correspondingly complex - with a particular focus on the street space, the traffic mix and the characteristic surroundings.

The replication of the track areas and the central station is one of the larger implementations in the Hamburg City-Map.
We already have an entry about the central station in the developer diary, which is linked below.

Our goal is to create the most vivid, detailed image of Hamburg Central Station possible - a place that millions know and that you can experience in a completely new way in The Bus.

As always, we welcome your questions and suggestions at:
TheBus@halycon.info

See you next time - and have fun on your virtual commute through Hamburg!

As the sort of virtual tourist who plays American Truck Simulator largely for sightseeing, I am well up for the early access launch of The Bus yesterday. So please be patient, passengers, as we go on a necessary detour around my collection of Google Maps pins. Roadworks, you know. Swans nesting in the traffic lights, or something.
